title: How do you build a training matrix for a dental practice?
seoTitle: Training matrix for a dental practice
description: Build a dental practice training matrix: bloodborne pathogens, infection control, radiation licensing, privacy, CPD and opioid training by role and market.
shortAnswer: A dental practice training matrix is built by listing each person in the practice, from dentists and hygienists to assistants, sterilization staff and reception, against the infection control, bloodborne pathogens, chemical safety, privacy, radiation and professional development rules that apply where the practice operates. Each cell records whether the duty is annual, event driven or one-time, and the evidence an inspector, board or accreditor would ask to see.
keyTakeaways: Dental work has its own triggers in general rules: OSHA treats saliva in dental procedures as potentially infectious material, so most clinical staff need annual bloodborne pathogens training.
Duties split between the practice and the practitioner. OSHA, HIPAA and accreditation duties sit with the practice; CPD, license renewal courses and DEA attestations sit with the individual.
Australia's Dental Board retired its infection control guidelines on 1 July 2022, so practices must now show their own system and training rather than point to a manual.
Some dental cells are one-time or multi-year: the DEA MATE Act training is a single 8 hour total, and Australian dental CPD is 60 hours over three years.
As at November 2026, the hazard communication deadline of November 20, 2026 and the NSW radiation changes for dental imaging are the near-term changes to build in.

sections.heading: Why does a dental practice need more than an infection control checklist?

blocks.text: Because infection control is only one of six or seven regimes that reach a dental team, and each has a different owner, clock and evidence rule. A practice can have spotless reprocessing and still fail an inspection because reception staff were never trained on privacy policies or because a training record is missing a required element.

The general approach in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) fits a dental practice well: people down the side, obligations across the top, a rule in every cell. The dental adaptation is to flag every person by exposure (clinical or non-clinical), by registration (registered practitioner or not) and by equipment use (radiography, cone beam CT), because those three flags decide most rows. Practices in a hospital setting should cross-check the [hospital training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix-for-a-hospital).

sections.heading: What does each market require of a dental practice?

blocks.text: Draw the columns from the regulation pages for each country and state where the practice operates. The summaries below use only facts recorded on those pages.

items: **United States, federal workplace rules.** 29 CFR 1910.1030 treats saliva in dental procedures as other potentially infectious material and exposed ends of dental wires as contaminated sharps. Training is free, during working hours, at initial assignment and at least annually within one year of the previous session, with 14 minimum elements including live questions and answers ([bloodborne pathogens](/regulations/osha-bloodborne-pathogens-training-requirements)). 29 CFR 1910.1200(h) requires chemical hazard training at initial assignment and when a new hazard is introduced ([dental office OSHA and HIPAA](/regulations/dental-office-osha-and-hipaa-training-requirements)).

**United States, privacy.** 45 CFR 164.530(b) requires privacy policy training for the workforce and 164.308(a)(5) requires a security awareness and training program for all workforce members including management, with documentation kept six years ([HIPAA training](/regulations/hipaa-security-and-privacy-training)).

**United States, controlled substances.** The Medication Access and Training Expansion (MATE) Act requires DEA registered practitioners, other than those who are solely veterinarians, to complete a one-time total of 8 hours of substance use disorder training, attested on the first registration application or renewal submitted on or after June 27, 2023 ([DEA MATE Act](/regulations/dea-mate-act-training-requirement)).

**California.** 16 CCR 1005 requires a written protocol for instrument processing, operatory cleanliness and management of injuries, made available to all dental health care personnel, and a copy of the regulation posted in each office. 16 CCR 1016(b)(1) lists Board-approved infection control, the Dental Practice Act, basic life support and Schedule II opioid prescribing among the mandatory renewal courses.

**Florida.** Section 456.0341 required a one-time 1 hour human trafficking course by January 1, 2021 for the listed professions, which include dentists ([human trafficking training](/regulations/human-trafficking-training-requirements-healthcare)).

**Australia.** Registered dental practitioners must follow the shared Code of conduct and the blood-borne virus guidelines and maintain infection prevention and control knowledge, which can count toward CPD. The dental CPD standard requires at least 60 hours over a three-year cycle, 48 clinically or scientifically based ([dental infection control](/regulations/dental-practice-infection-control-training-australia), [Ahpra CPD](/regulations/ahpra-cpd-registration-standards)). In South Australia, dentists are prescribed health practitioners who must report suspected risk to a child ([mandatory reporting](/regulations/mandatory-reporting-training-australia)). In NSW, anyone using regulated radiation apparatus needs a radiation user licence unless an exemption applies ([radiation licence](/regulations/radiation-safety-licence-training-australia)).

sections.heading: How should infection control training be evidenced without a prescribed manual?

blocks.text: Map each infection control obligation to a learning outcome and a piece of evidence the practice holds, because in Australia there is no longer a Board manual to point to. On notification, the Dental Board may ask about the practice's processes and sources and may inspect the place of practice.

sections.heading: Which dental clocks are fixed, and which does the practice choose?

blocks.text: The fixed clocks come from OSHA, the DEA and the boards; most others are left to the practice. Label each cell with its source so that a chosen interval is visibly a choice.

items: **Annual by rule.** Bloodborne pathogens training must recur within one year of the previous session, and the exposure control plan must be reviewed at least annually.
**Event driven.** Hazard communication follows a new chemical hazard; HIPAA privacy training follows a material policy change; bloodborne pathogens training is repeated when tasks change exposure.

**Multi-year or one-time.** Australian dental CPD runs over a three-year cycle. MATE training is one-time, and practitioner DEA registrations expire 36 months from the initial expiration date, which sets when the attestation falls due. NSW radiation user licences are valid for 1 or 3 years.

**Chosen by the practice.** The Dental Board no longer prescribes an infection control manual or interval, and HIPAA sets no annual frequency. Record the reason for each chosen cycle; [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) sets out a method.

sections.heading: Which dental rule changes fall in 2025 to 2027?

blocks.text: Enter these as dated rows so cells change status on the right day. As at November 2026, the regulation pages record:

items: **1 December 2025, NSW:** an exemption for dental OPG and lateral cephalometric imaging applies under the Protection from Harmful Radiation Regulation 2025, but a license is still needed for cone beam CT.

**15 May to 17 July 2026, Australia:** Ahpra and 14 National Boards consulted on revised recency of practice and CPD standards. The Dental Board currently requires 60 hours over three years; the draft proposes 20 hours a year, with substantial notice before any change.
**1 September 2026, NSW:** radiation management plans fell due under the 2025 Regulation.
**20 November 2026, United States:** employers must update hazard communication programs and training for newly identified hazards in substances; mixtures follow on May 19, 2028.

blocks.title: Watch items
blocks.text: The 2025 Dental Code is not yet in the National Directory for Radiation Protection, and the January 2025 HIPAA Security Rule proposal for training at least every 12 months had no final rule as at the HIPAA page's last review. Track both before changing matrix rows.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry links each dental obligation to the people it applies to, the learning outcome it requires and the assessment point that evidences it, so infection control, radiation and privacy duties can be shown to an inspector from one structure. When a rule such as the NSW radiation exemptions changes, the affected rows are flagged. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Do dental assistants need annual bloodborne pathogens training?
faqs.a: In the United States, yes, where their tasks involve occupational exposure. OSHA's definition of other potentially infectious materials includes saliva in dental procedures, so most chairside assistants are in scope and must be trained at initial assignment and within one year of their previous session.

faqs.q: Is infection control training still required in Australia after the Dental Board guidelines were retired?
faqs.a: Yes. Retiring the guidelines removed a prescribed manual, not the duty. Practitioners must still prevent or minimize infection, follow the Code of conduct and blood-borne virus guidelines and maintain their knowledge, and accredited practices must evidence workforce training under the Clinical Safety Standard.

faqs.q: Does a dentist repeat the MATE Act training at every DEA renewal?
faqs.a: No. It is a one-time total of 8 hours, attested on the first application or renewal submitted on or after June 27, 2023, and it is not part of future renewals. Training completed before the Act, and earlier DATA waiver training, can count.

faqs.q: Who in a dental practice needs HIPAA training?
faqs.a: Every workforce member of a dental practice that is a HIPAA covered entity, including employees, volunteers, trainees and management. Reception and billing staff need privacy policy training as much as clinicians, and the practice must document it and keep the records for six years.
